subject: Clarify DPA incident-notification & cooperation expectations
messages:
From: Sara Howell <sara.howell@acme-payments.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: James Park <james.park@acme-payments.com>; Priyanka Das <priyanka.das@acme-payments.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify DPA incident-notification & cooperation expectations

Hi Irene —

Thanks for taking this. As part of our procurement review at Acme Payments we need to confirm the practical commitments Redwood makes around privacy incidents (DPA/SCC context). A few points we need clarity on before legal will sign: 

1) Notification timeline: our regulators expect initial notification to the controller within 48 hours of becoming aware of a personal data breach. Your standard DPA references "as soon as reasonably practicable" and the SOC2 playbook mentions 72 hours for confirmed incidents. Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to an express 48-hour initial notification for incidents that reasonably may affect Acme data? If there are exceptions, please list them.

2) Scope of information: Acme will need, at minimum, the categories of personal data affected, estimated number of records, and the likely timeframe of exposure. Please confirm what level of detail Redwood can provide in the initial notice vs follow-up reports.

3) Cooperation & evidence: We will expect Redwood to assist with forensic analysis, provide logs and artifacts, and preserve evidence for regulatory review. Please state any limitations (e.g., sharing other customers' metadata, redaction practices, legal process required).

4) SCCs/HIPAA/DPIA support: we may need assistance mapping SCCs and producing DPIA evidence (data flows, subprocessors). Please confirm contacts and typical lead times.

Can you send your SOC 2 executive summary and incident playbook excerpt under NDA? I'm attaching a short checklist of our incident evidence requirements to help align.

Appreciate a point-by-point response today if possible — procurement needs this to move to legal.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Howell
Head of Vendor Risk — Acme Payments
Attach: Acme_incident_requirements_checklist.xlsx

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Sara Howell <sara.howell@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify DPA incident-notification & cooperation expectations

Hi Sara —

Thanks for the clear checklist. Quick summary up front: we understand Acme's regulatory constraints and are prepared to negotiate a tailored notification and cooperation section; below is our standard position and proposed practical commitments. Karthik and Marissa are looped in for legal/ops specifics.

1) Notification timeline
- Redwood's default operational policy: initial internal detection notification is "as soon as reasonably practicable," with confirmed personal-data-impact notices typically issued within 72 hours of becoming aware.
- We can commit to an accelerated initial notice for named customers where the evidence suggests their data may be impacted. For a contracted commitment, we can offer: 
  a) Initial notification of suspected personal data impact: best efforts within 48 hours of becoming aware;
  b) If confirmation requires longer forensic work, we will provide an interim notice within 48 hours with available facts and a status update;
  c) Final incident report within 30 days for operational details and remediation steps (or a different mutually agreed timeline).
- Exceptions: delays required to conduct criminal investigations, law-enforcement requests, or where immediate disclosure would materially prejudice remediation or the security of other customers. Any delay will be documented and communicated.

2) Scope of initial info
- Initial notice will include: nature of the incident, suspected data categories affected, estimated scope (records/identifiers where available), detection timestamp, and immediate mitigations in place. Precise record counts may be estimated initially and refined.

3) Cooperation & evidence
- Redwood will: preserve relevant logs, provide timeline summaries, and share sanitized forensic artifacts and query results. We will not share other customers' raw data; cross-customer metadata will be redacted.
- For detailed logs/host-level artifacts that could include other customers' data, Redwood requests a narrow, scoped request and, where necessary, a lawful process (e.g., NDA + DPA amendment or subpoena).
- We can provide a named liaison from our incident response team and support law- or regulatory-facing evidence packages under a data-sharing agreement.

4) SCCs/DPIA/HIPAA support
- We will provide mapping to SCCs and assist with DPIA artifacts (data flow diagrams, subprocessors, data retention notes) on a commercial level — typical turnaround 5–10 business days for standard packages.
- For HIPAA applicability, Redwood is not currently a HIPAA-covered entity by default; we support Business Associate Agreements in scope-limited deployments. If Acme expects HIPAA-covered processing, let's clarify use cases and environment (private deployment vs hosted).

Attachments: SOC2 executive summary and a short incident playbook excerpt (redacted for other customers) are in this thread. We can also drop a redline of the DPA with suggested language for the 48-hour interim notice and cooperation scope.

Proposed next step: If Acme can accept "initial interim notice within 48 hours with best-effort details, final report within 30 days," we'll work with legal to produce redline DPA language and service-level commitments. If you need an absolute 48-hour guaranteed contractual SLA for all incidents, we'll need to scope that as a Dedicated or Private deployment option with operational commitments and potential pricing impact.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
Attachments: SOC2_TypeII_executive_summary.pdf; incident_playbook_summary.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sara Howell <sara.howell@acme-payments.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify DPA incident-notification & cooperation expectations

Sara/Irene —

Adding a proposed set of DPA clauses we use internally that balance regulator expectations with operational realities. High level recommendations: 

- Initial notice: "Seller shall use commercially reasonable efforts to provide Customer an initial notice within 48 hours of Seller becoming aware of a security incident that reasonably may affect Customer's personal data. If Seller is unable to provide the required detail within 48 hours due to ongoing investigation or law enforcement involvement, Seller shall provide an interim notice and reasonably estimated timeframe for a follow-up report."

- Evidence limits: "Seller shall provide logs, timeline reconstructions, and sanitized forensic artifacts necessary for Customer's regulatory submissions. Seller shall not disclose other customers' PII; requests for raw artifacts that may contain third-party data shall require prior agreement or lawful process."

- Cooperation: "Seller shall designate a single point of contact, participate in joint technical calls, and reasonably cooperate with Customer's regulatory counsel and appointed forensic firms. Cooperation does not include redirecting Seller's internal resources in a manner that materially impacts service to other customers without commercially reasonable compensation."

- Remedies: propose to avoid per-incident financial penalties in the initial public DPA; reserve contractual remedies for material breaches tied to gross negligence. Operational remedies include prioritized support and dedicated investigation staffing under a paid plan.

I've attached a redline with these clauses (DPA_redline_v1.docx). Happy to walk through specifics.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Legal (Commercial Contracts) | Redwood Inference
Attachment: DPA_redline_v1.docx

From: Sara Howell <sara.howell@acme-payments.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: James Park <james.park@acme-payments.com>, Priyanka Das <priyanka.das@acme-payments.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify DPA incident-notification & cooperation expectations

Irene/Karthik —

Thank you — this is helpful and closer to what we need. A couple of follow-ups from our side: 

- Regulator stance: for payment processors in our EU footprint, the 48-hour window is a firm expectation. An interim notice (even if high-level) at 48 hours is acceptable; Acme will push back on language that makes 48 hours purely "best efforts." For contract flexibility, Acme can accept a limited set of exceptions (law enforcement, active remediation where disclosure would materially worsen impact).

- Scope detail at 48 hours: we require categories of personal data, an estimated number of affected records (range ok), and whether credentials/payment instruments are implicated. If you can't state counts, an upper-bound estimate is acceptable.

- Evidence: Acme's regulator may request raw logs; please confirm Redwood's process for producing logs that may contain other customers' metadata. If production requires a narrow warrant/subpoena route, we need that documented.

Next steps: we will ask legal to take your redline and produce a counter-redline to the DPA this week. Can Redwood confirm a named incident liaison and contact details we can rely on in an incident? Also, please confirm whether the SOC2 summary and incident playbook will be shared under the mutual NDA we executed earlier — we can't advance without that evidence.

I'll await the liaison name and the redline DPA language. If you can provide a brief paragraph committing to the 48-hour interim notice (with exceptions described) we can move to countersignature.

Best,
Sara
Attach: Acme_incident_requirements_checklist.xlsx (previously attached)
